absent: Write-side validation and effects of guest control handler referenced by the descriptor table
Layout locking and side effects of virtual control fetch and store helpers
Host and guest trap description derivation and EL2 enable constant value
Generic system register user helpers descriptor lookup and hidden-state checks
Locking if any around system register user accesses and VMCR updates
Full distributor and ITS object layouts and interrupt lookup reference rules
Meaning of maintenance status bits and configured maintenance identifier selection
IRQ file-descriptor routing entry layout lazy init failure modes and injection target rules

findings.text: Guest control view combines per-CPU priority width and identifier width with host trap feature bits and current virtual control values for common binary point and end-of-interrupt mode.
Priority mask, binary point zero and both group enables behave as masked views of one virtual control record that is fetched and stored back with a single field changed on each user write.
Binary point one depends on common flag: when clear it stores and returns its own alternate value, when set writes are ignored and reads report the other binary point plus one capped at seven.
Active priority state lives in two per-CPU indexed arrays selected by a group flag, with helpers choosing array zero or one and the caller supplied slot.
User active priority accesses derive slot from low two bits of the encoding second opcode and reject slots above a priority-width dependent maximum.
Maximum active priority index is three with seven priority bits, one with six priority bits, otherwise zero, so it is usable before control restore.
EL1 enable writes must request enablement or fail, while reads return the stored per-CPU value unchanged.
EL2 enable and trap description values are immutable from userspace: only exact matches to expected constants are accepted and reads always return those constants.
Generic EL2 interface registers are stored directly in per-vCPU system register storage indexed by descriptor and returned unchanged.

A static descriptor table binds guest priority, binary point, active priority, control, enable and group controls plus nested EL2 interface controls to their user handlers; EL2 entries are hidden unless nested virtualization is enabled for the vCPU.

Attribute probe translates KVM VGIC encoding fields to an internal identifier and reports presence only when a visible descriptor exists; read and write paths build a one-register request and delegate to generic user helpers sized by the descriptor table.
Distributor debug iterator carries CPU count, shared interrupt count, distributor phase flag, current vCPU number and current interrupt identifier.

Debug walk starts with a distributor slot, then cycles private identifiers across online vCPUs, then shared identifiers in order, then present low power interrupts in ascending order, ending past the largest allowed identifier.
ITS debug position is a device pointer plus a translation entry pointer, with both null meaning end of iteration.

ITS advance stays inside the current device table until its last entry, then moves to the next device first entry, terminating with a null pair after the final device; start seeds the first pair and skips by file offset.
Interrupt state printing holds the per-interrupt raw spinlock with interrupts saved while formatting one row and releases it afterwards.
ITS debug walk holds the ITS mutex from sequence start until stop, including offset skipping and early termination paths.
Low power interrupt enumeration and counting scan the distributor key-value store under read-side critical sections.

Distributor summary reports model variant, shared count, low power count for v3 only, enable state and a flag legend; per-interrupt rows classify type by identifier range and refresh pending state from host for hardware software-generated interrupts.

ITS output prints a device header once per device with identifier and event range derived from event bit width, then one line per translation with event, interrupt, hardware, target, collection and hardware flag only when both interrupt and collection are linked.
ITS debug file is created under the VM debug directory with read-only permissions and a base-address derived name; teardown performs no action.
Default maintenance interrupt identifier is twenty five.
VGIC tracing uses subsystem kvm with a vgic trace include path and file plus a once-only include guard.

Maintenance signaling may arrive asynchronously so general folding is deferred to the exit path; the handler always reports handled and only in nested state injects a virtual maintenance level and disables interface enable.
Nested maintenance handling samples the missed-status level, injects the configured maintenance identifier at that level, then clears interface enable.
Global platform GIC information is installed once at early init and rejects a second install by allocating and copying the caller record.
IRQ file-descriptor path converts a routing pin to a shared identifier by adding the private count, validates shared range, ensures lazy initialization, then injects the requested level.

Out-of-range active priority slots, cleared enable requests and mismatched EL2 fixed values fail user writes; unknown or hidden attributes fail probe with no such device; iterator allocation failure returns an encoded no-memory error.
